claim.why_it_matters: The sibling statement clauses on the preceding pages are '## 4.5 THE READ STATEMENT', '## 4.6 THE REWRITE STATEMENT', '## 4.7 THE START STATEMENT' with '### 4.x.y' subheadings; 4.8 and its subclauses are demoted one level, so a heading-based outline nests the USE statement under START instead of beside it.

verdict.reasoning: Printed page 465 (VIII-35, Relative I-O) sets '4.8 THE USE STATEMENT' and 4.8.1-4.8.4 in the same typographic style as 4.5 READ, 4.6 REWRITE, 4.7 START and 4.9 WRITE. In specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md those siblings are '## 4.5', '## 4.6', '## ║4.7 ...║', '## 4.9' with '### 4.x.y' subclauses, but 4.8 is '### 4.8 THE USE STATEMENT' with '#### 4.8.1'-'#### 4.8.4'. The heading text is all present; the defect is the one-level demotion, which makes a heading-derived outline nest 4.8 under 4.7 START. That is a structural defect in the transcription, not page furniture, so the claim stands; only the kind label 'missing-heading' is inaccurate (the headings are present, at the wrong level).
verdict.corrected_description: Heading-level defect, not a missing heading: in the Relative I-O module, '4.8 THE USE STATEMENT' is transcribed at level ### (subclauses 4.8.1-4.8.4 at ####) while its siblings 4.5, 4.6, 4.7 and 4.9 are at ## (subclauses at ###). The printed page gives 4.8 the same rank as its siblings; promote 4.8 to ## and 4.8.1-4.8.4 to ###.
